The nine pins, all driven through the injected platform/nowMs/uptimeSeconds seams so a Linux or macOS host runs the win32 branch (whole-minute inputs; boot minute 29999880):
1. Registration: win32 records pid plus the floored boot minute in processStartId; +59.999 s same minute, +60 s next minute; no runtime for an absent pid, platform darwin, or unusable clock inputs (negative or NaN uptime, NaN now, minute 0).
2. Opt-in versus default: default is "unavailable" with no probable key; opted in is "live" with probable: true and exactly five keys, no nonce; only literal true opts in (1, "true", {}, undefined, null, false all stay unavailable); darwin stays unavailable opted in, registered or read there.
3. Tolerance edge: deltas 0, -1, -60000, +59999, +60000, +119999 ms read live/probable; -60001, -120000, +120000 read reused, no probable key.
4. Reused versus not-live: a rebooted host (uptime reset) reads reused (default read unavailable); a descriptor rewritten to a vanished pid reads not-live with and without opt-in, never probable.
5. Host table on the real platform: Linux live/live with no probable key; win32 unavailable default, live+probable opted in; other hosts unavailable both ways.
6. Warning shape via the inspectOwner seam: exactly six keys, schema constant, status live, probable true, message matches "probably live", no nonce/processStartId/boot minute; the warning opts in and pins the descriptor digest; on real Linux the warning keeps its four-key shape.
7. Warning edge: fires at -60000..+119999 ms, silent at -120000, -60001, +120000, after a reboot, and for a vanished owner.
8. Retirement family: inspectSessionRetirement reads owner-unavailable, inspectExternallyArchivedSession owner-active, inspectOrphanArchiveEligibility ownerStatus unavailable (not asserted beyond that); none carries a probable marker.
9. Structural: only lib/worktree-lifecycle.mjs and scripts/pipeline-start-preflight.mjs mention probableLiveness among non-test .mjs files under lib, scripts and hooks.

4. Deliberately not changed
- Every production file, the D0 session-owner test (it still pins unavailable off Linux), the CSW-T pins, and the foreign uncommitted edits in pipeline-state.mjs, po-human-approval.mjs, sanctioned-args-onboarding.mjs and pipeline-state.test.mjs (the index still holds two of them staged; I committed by exact pathspec only).
- consumer-safe-paths was not run: it is not in this slice's DoD (CSW-F recorded a pre-existing red in the ADR-0014 copy).

5. Deviations from spec
- None to the goal or DoD. Pin 9 (the structural scan) is the one design choice beyond the literal bullet list: it is how "retirement never acts on a probable status" is made checkable, since the claim rests on no retirement caller opting in.
- I did not pin the behavior of forwarding probableLiveness into the retirement readers (see open items), because that is not a claim the landed design makes.
- No before-run exists: the pins cover already-landed code, so there is no red baseline by construction.

6. Open items
- Observation, not a defect today: inspectSessionRetirement, inspectExternallyArchivedSession and inspectOrphanArchiveEligibility spread ...options into the owner read. A caller that forwarded probableLiveness: true would get a probably-live owner as owner-live/owner-active/observable (the blocking direction), but a boot-minute mismatch ("reused") would make inspectSessionRetirement answer "retirable". Pin 9 keeps that unreachable; if a retirement caller ever opts in, the option should be stripped there first.
- Observation: on win32 the default read of a probably live owner is "unavailable", and "unavailable" is in ORPHAN_ARCHIVE_OWNER_STATUSES. That is unchanged by CSW-F (it was unavailable before), but it means the zero-authority orphan-archive tier does not see a live native-Windows owner as observable. I asserted only ownerStatus there and did not measure the eligibility verdict; a follow-up slice may want to decide whether that is intended.
- Still unverified (carried from CSW-F): whether os.uptime() on Windows counts time asleep; if not, the boot minute drifts after each sleep and a live session reads "reused" (a quiet miss).
- The Linux-only four-key warning assertion ran on WSL only; the native run took the win32 branch of the host table (the native session registered and read within one minute of each other).
